- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is negative (especially > -0.40) — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior day’s close.
- Underestimate price spikes in late forecast windows when sentiment turns positive (especially > 0.03) — add 1–2% buffer to forecasted peak.
- Lagged forecasts (e.g., 10+ days ahead) consistently overpredict by 1–3% — apply 1.5x smoothing or decay factor to reduce bias.
- When sentiment is persistently negative (avg < -0.30 over 5 days), reduce forecast mean by 1–2% and shift peak to later horizon.
- Avoid overreacting to recent sentiment spikes — if sentiment > 0.10 for 3+ consecutive days, cap forecast increase at 1.5x prior peak.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is > 2.5% above 14-day moving average, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overshoot by 1–3% in early weeks — apply 1.2x decay to first 7 days of forecast.
